1.pericope_label: Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee

debates.q: What does the title word, destroy not, refer to?

sides.view: A divine warning spoken to David in the cave, afterwards adopted as the title
Rather God’s limit on Saul — persecute, but do not destroy him
Pure conjecture; three explanations are current and none can be settled
Nothing historical — it names the melody the psalm is to be sung to
The title points to the end, which is Christ, and the psalm sings the Passion

debates.q: What does God send from heaven?

sides.view: Angels, with the Targum and Kimchi — though the point is that help comes from above, not from men
Angels if need be, or simply the command; and mercy and truth as personified messengers
His gracious help in pursuance of his promises
The verb stands absolutely; the second clause should read rebuke, not reproach

outliers.view: Treats the psalm title as the transcript of an interruption — the words that stopped David killing Saul, kept and used as a heading

4.pericope_label: My soul is among lions: and I lie even among them that are set on fire

debates.q: Is the soul among lions, or in parched places?

sides.view: In parched places — an emendation from a root meaning to thirst, which the Chaldee seems to support
Among lions, meaning Saul and his three thousand chosen men
Among lions, and the second phrase means greedy ones, literally lickers

debates.q: Can the sixth verse be repaired?

sides.view: No — the parallelism is hopelessly lost, and Ewald’s conjecture defies the grammar without restoring it
Nothing needs repairing; the verse is a hunter’s picture fulfilled in Saul walking into the cave
The snares are the insidious ways used to get David into their hands

outliers.view: Repeats the rabbinic tale of the spider that webbed the cave mouth and so saved David, then backs it with English, Greek and Latin proverbs on the trapper trapped

7.pericope_label: My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise

debates.q: What is the glory that must awake?

sides.view: The soul, which can sleep when grace is dormant or sorrow presses it down
Not the soul but the harp — a manuscript and the Syriac read the instrument
The tongue, the instrument of singing
The noblest powers together: intellect, tongue and imagination

debates.q: Does the singer wake early, or wake the dawn?

sides.view: He rouses the dawn, as the cock calls forth the morning in the poets
He wakes himself, rousing every power for the hour of praise

outliers.view: Declines to dismiss the rabbinic tale of the harp that played by itself in the north wind, and asks whether it describes an instrument answering to the wind-played harp lately rediscovered
Explains the overlap with another psalm as a copying accident — notes from the psalmist’s diary transcribed twice
